title: Supplier Temporary Credentials & Access Evidence Runbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This runbook is a working draft describing recommended contractual language, operational controls, and evidence artifacts we should require when vendors or suppliers are granted temporary (ephemeral) credentials into any Redwood-managed environment. The focus is on minimizing blast radius, ensuring timely revocation, and having concrete artifacts for audits.

Scope:
Applies to: third-party professional-services engineers, contractor-run automation, vendor troubleshooting sessions, and short-lived CI/CD access used by external suppliers. Not intended for long-term managed vendor service accounts (those are covered by separate on-boarding).

Quick summary of risk model:
- Ephemeral credentials reduce long-lived secret risk but can still be abused if not constrained (excess permissions, long TTL, network access).
- Primary controls: narrow scopes, forced rotation, short TTL, cryptographically-authenticated sessions (OIDC/STS), enforced session tagging/logging, and immediate revocation hooks.

Recommended contract language (examples to copy into SOW / DPA / vendor agreement):
1) Ephemeral Access Principle: "Supplier shall only use temporary, short-lived credentials for access to Customer environments. Long-lived credentials are prohibited unless expressly approved in writing and subject to monthly justification and rotation."
2) Least Privilege and Justification: "Each access grant must include a scoped justification, an expiration timestamp, and an assigned Redwood requestor owner. Supplier shall request elevation only via documented change control tickets."
3) Rotation & TTL: "All ephemeral credentials must expire automatically within a maximum of 8 hours for interactive sessions and 24 hours for automation CRON/jobs, unless a shorter TTL is specified in the access grant."
4) Evidence & Logs: "Supplier must provide, on request, signed session manifests, unique session identifiers, and any command-level transcripts generated during the access window. Supplier consents to Redwood access to audit logs and session recordings held by the Supplier."
5) Revocation & Emergency Measures: "Redwood may revoke any issued credential immediately. Supplier shall implement and test automatic revocation hooks (webhooks or API calls) to invalidate active sessions within 60 seconds of request."

Operational controls (implementation notes / checklist):
- Use OIDC + STS or short-lived SSH certificates instead of static keys.
- Enforce strong session labels/tags: requester, ticket id, reason, expiry, environment, and change-id.
- Network segmentation: supplier sessions should originate from restricted egress ranges or through an approved jump host with packet capture enabled for the session.
- Command auditing: force shell session recording (TTY-level) or use a bastion that records session activity. Keep artifacts for at least 90 days for higher-risk customers.
- MFA requirement for supplier consoles and for remote access initiation.
- Automatic TTL enforcement via central identity provider; deny issuance if requested TTL > allowed max.
- Credentials issuance flow should require approval from a named Redwood approver for sensitive scopes.

Evidence checklist sent to procurement / audit (minimum set):
- Access request (ticket id and approval email).
- Session manifest (session id, start/end, principal, ephemeral token id).
- Signed command transcript OR bastion recording reference (S3/secure storage path).
- IP addresses and ASN of source connections.
- List of resources accessed (ARNs, db names, bucket names) and operations performed.
- Proof of revocation (revocation API response or token introspection showing invalidated token).
- Supplier attestation (signed statement: no copies retained, no lateral access beyond scope).

Vendor security assessment questions (for intake form / SVA):
- Do you use temporary credentials (OIDC/STS) for external access? If not, why?
- What is the maximum TTL you allow for interactive and automation credentials?
- Describe how you enforce least privilege for temporary sessions.
- Do you support session recording and retrieval on request? For how long are recordings retained?
- Describe your revocation process and expected time-to-revoke on API call.
- Do you provide signed manifests or HMAC-signed artifacts proving session integrity?
- Which cloud regions and IP ranges will supplier-originated sessions come from?

Sample technical SLA for credentials (to include as annex):
- Provisioning latency: 95th percentile issuance < 2 minutes after approval.
- Revocation latency: 90% < 10s, 99% < 60s from API call.
- Audit artifact availability: session manifests and recordings accessible within 24 hours on request; retained for minimum 90 days (or 365 days for regulated customers).

Redlines and negotiation notes (things legal usually push back on):
- Supplier pushback: "We cannot guarantee sub-60s revocation for all environments (multi-cloud)" -> Acceptable counter: require API-based revocation and additional network-level session termination on exit nodes; document exceptions and escalate to customer SRE for design acceptance.
- Supplier pushback: "We retain session recordings for operational debugging" -> Counter: require encryption with customer KEK or redaction, or restrict retention to agreed time window and delete scripts with attestation.

Open questions / TODOs: 
- Decide default TTL for automation (propose 4h) and interactive (2h) across product teams.
- Add templated RBAC roles for common troubleshooting tasks to avoid ad-hoc permission grants.
- Define retention tiers by risk level (90 / 180 / 365 days).
- Work with infra team to prototype a webhook revocation test harness (see jira:SEC-4217).

Evidence formatting examples (copyable):
- Session manifest (one-line JSON signed with supplier key): {session_id: "s-123456", start: "2024-11-20T16:12:00Z", end: "2024-11-20T16:34:00Z", subject: "vendor:acme-support", ticket: "RD-2419", resources: ["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-prod-logs"], signature: "base64sig"}

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive — aim is to move vendor onboarding to ephemeral-first by default. Expect significant pushback for legacy managed-services.
- Ask solutions-eng to create sample terraform/okta/pike scripts for one-click issuance flow; then we can convert to a supplier-runbook artifact for SOW attachments.

Relevant links / references: confluence:SEC-EPHEMERAL-REFERENCE, jira:SEC-4217 (revocation harness), github:infra/ephemeral-creds-pr-88

Status: draft — prefer product + infra + legal sync to finalize clause language and technical feasibility.

Owner (action items):
- Asha: consolidate feedback and make v0.1 legal-ready draft by 2024-11-29.
- Liam: prototype revocation webhook proof-of-concept (due 2024-11-15).
- Maya: map existing supplier contracts and flag ones requiring retroactive addendum.

End of document.
